subject.title: fix(setup): validate current OpenClaw package lifecycle

question: Should Windows Companion make official OpenClaw `2026.7.1` its production LKG before the current PR head has demonstrated a successful official-package setup and Gateway-health run?
rationale: This is a default-selection and upgrade-safety choice affecting ordinary onboarding, not a mechanical implementation detail. The composed-candidate digest proof validates a different package path and cannot decide whether the production default is acceptable.

options.title: Require official-default proof or retain the prior LKG
options.body: Keep the integrity changes, but do not change the normal default until an exact-head official-package setup run proves install, configuration, service health, and pairing.

options.title: Accept the known setup risk
options.body: Merge the newer LKG now and explicitly accept that some first-run users may need recovery while the official-path failure is resolved upstream.

options.title: Split the release-selection change
options.body: Land only the digest-bound composed-package path in a narrower PR and review the LKG update separately when its official runtime proof is available.

recommendation.title: Require official-default proof or retain the prior LKG
recommendation.body: Keep the integrity changes, but do not change the normal default until an exact-head official-package setup run proves install, configuration, service health, and pairing.

likelyOwner.reason: CassieMei authored the supplied commits that introduced the LKG, package, lifecycle, and compatibility behavior, though current-main ownership could not be verified in this environment.
